extracted.intended_audience: covered entities under section 1557 (health programs and activities, health care providers, health insurance issuers, Exchanges, CMS and HHS OCR staff)
extracted.subtask_description: Final rule implementing Section 1557 of the Affordable Care Act setting nondiscrimination obligations for health programs and activities and amending CMS regulations. Specifies substantive prohibitions (race, color, national origin, sex, age, disability) and a suite of procedural, notice, training, accessibility, data, benefit-design, and enforcement requirements for covered entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and Effective Date (§92.1)
rubrics_metrics.description: The purpose of 45 CFR part 92 is to implement section 1557, prohibiting discrimination in certain health programs and activities on grounds adopted from title VI, title IX, the Age Act, and section 504. The overall effective date is 60 days after publication, with phased-in applicability dates for provisions requiring changes to health insurance or group health plan benefit design and certain procedural requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR maintains a 60-day effective date for the general prohibition but adopts delayed applicability for procedural requirements (e.g., designation of coordinator, policies and procedures, training, notices) and delayed applicability of benefit-design requirements (first day of the first plan year beginning on or after January 1, 2025) for coverage newly subject to the rule. OCR declined to provide broad safe harbors but allowed phased compliance timelines to permit covered entities time to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application / Covered Entities (§92.2 and general)
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule applies to 'covered entities' defined collectively as recipients of Federal financial assistance, the Department, and title I entities (entities established under title I of the ACA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities receiving Federal financial assistance or administering programs identified in section 1557 must comply with the nondiscrimination obligations and related procedural requirements in this part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relationship to Other Laws (§92.3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Section 1557 adopts the grounds of discrimination from title VI, title IX, the Age Act, and section 504; enforcement mechanisms provided under those statutes apply to violations of section 1557.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory interpretation and enforcement will be coordinated with existing civil rights statutes and regulations; agencies should ensure consistency across regimes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions (§92.4)
rubrics_metrics.description: Includes new and revised definitions (e.g., telehealth, State, relay interpretation, patient care decision support tools) and changes phrasing (e.g., 'individual with limited English proficiency' replacing 'limited English proficient individual').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions clarify scope and application (for example, expanding definition to include companions with LEP in some contexts) and affect how provisions like meaningful access and ICT accessibility are applied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurances Required (§92.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients of Federal financial assistance must provide assurances required by the rule as a condition of receiving assistance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paperwork Reduction Act ICRs cover assurances; assurances tie program funding to compliance obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial Action and Voluntary Action (§92.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities are expected to take remedial action when discrimination occurs and may undertake voluntary actions to address disparities and accessibility needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provision frames accountability and incentives for corrective steps but specifics depend on enforcement and the facts of individual complaints.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation and Responsibilities of a Section 1557 Coordinator (§92.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities (subject to the requirements) must designate a Section 1557 Coordinator responsible for coordinating compliance efforts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR adopted phased applicability allowing time to designate coordinators; duties include coordinating policies/procedures, retention of grievance records, and other documentation. Estimated compliance burdens (time/hours) are discussed in Regulatory Impact Analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policies and Procedures (§92.8)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must develop and maintain nondiscrimination policies and procedures, including grievance procedures, language access procedures, effective communication procedures, and reasonable modification procedures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR recognized commenters' concerns about timing and complexity and provided phased applicability dates to allow tailoring of policies; entities should ensure procedures address notice, grievance handling, documentation, and accessibility in line with the rule's substantive provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training (§92.9)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must provide and document training for relevant staff on section 1557 obligations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR acknowledges the burden on entities and estimated documentation time (e.g., 1.25 hours documenting employee training). Phased applicability allows time to implement training programs. Training should cover policies, notice requirements, language access, effective communication, and nondiscrimination standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Nondiscrimination (§92.10)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must publish and distribute a Notice of Nondiscrimination describing rights under section 1557.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requirements include content and dissemination expectations; the rule ties notice obligations to accessibility and language assistance notices described elsewhere in the part.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice of Availability of Language Assistance Services and Auxiliary Aids and Services (§92.11)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires a Notice of Availability informing individuals about language assistance services and auxiliary aids and services; this replaces the former 'tagline' requirement and explicitly includes auxiliary aids.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR revised applicability dates (delayed one year for Notice of Availability) to give covered entities time to comply. The notice must include auxiliary aids and services in addition to language assistance; taglines are not required under the final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Data Collection
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule requires certain data collection relevant to nondiscrimination obligations (referenced in table of contents and PRA discussion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paperwork Reduction Act analyses and information collection requests (ICRs) are associated with assurances, coordinator designation and training, and notice requirements; entities should follow ICR guidance and retain required records.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discrimination Prohibited (§92.101)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits discrimination on the basis of race, color, national origin, sex, age, or disability in a health program or activity that receives Federal financial assistance or is administered by an executive agency or title I entity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the central substantive prohibition; enforcement mechanisms from title VI, title IX, the Age Act, and section 504 apply. The preamble clarifies coverage and examples across programs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaningful Access for Individuals With Limited English Proficiency (§92.201)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must ensure meaningful access for individuals with limited English proficiency; the final rule adds 'companions with limited English proficiency' and adjusts guidance about interpreting modalities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR modified provisions to clarify that audio/video remote interpreting may not be appropriate in certain circumstances and to ensure parity with effective communication provisions; entities must consider context and appropriateness of interpreting modalities to provide meaningful access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective Communication for Individuals With Disabilities (§92.202)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must ensure effective communication with individuals with disabilities, including provision of auxiliary aids and services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule links this requirement to the Notice of Availability and to obligations to provide auxiliary aids unless an undue burden or fundamental alteration is demonstrated; specifics depend on individual needs and context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility for Buildings and Facilities (§92.203)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must ensure physical accessibility of buildings and facilities used in health programs and activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities should follow applicable architectural and program accessibility standards and make reasonable modifications to provide access consistent with the rule's nondiscrimination objectives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accessibility of Information and Communication Technology for Individuals With Disabilities (§92.204)
rubrics_metrics.description: Information and communication technology (ICT) used in health programs and activities must be accessible to individuals with disabilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This covers websites, portals, digital tools, and other ICT; entities must implement accessible ICT practices and may be subject to enforcement if ICT excludes individuals with disabilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement To Make Reasonable Modifications (§92.205)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities are required to make reasonable modifications to policies, practices, and procedures to avoid discrimination against individuals with disabilities, unless a requested modification would fundamentally alter the program or impose an undue burden.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities must evaluate modification requests individually and document reasons for any denials; reasonable modification obligations apply to both program access and provision of auxiliary aids/services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Equal Program Access on the Basis of Sex (§92.206)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits sex-based discrimination in program access; the final rule clarifies that covered entities may raise legitimate, nondiscriminatory reasons for denial of care, but the basis for denial must not be unlawful animus or bias or a pretext for discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR modified text to balance recognition of legitimate nondiscriminatory clinical or administrative reasons while prohibiting decisions grounded in animus, bias, or pretext; entities should document and justify nondiscriminatory reasons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination in Health Insurance Coverage and Other Health-Related Coverage (§92.207)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits discrimination in health insurance coverage and other health-related coverage, including restrictions on discriminatory benefit designs, and addresses scope of application (including exceptions like excepted benefits and STLDI), application to third party administrators, and network adequacy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR revised §92.207 to clarify covered entities may cite legitimate nondiscriminatory reasons for denials but prohibits pretextual reasons. Delayed applicability applies for newly covered health insurance coverage: benefit-design provisions apply first day of first plan year on/after January 1, 2025. Some aspects (b)(1)-(5) apply immediately to coverage already subject to the 2020 Rule (e.g., Medicare Advantage, Medicaid managed care). OCR will not enforce certain new categories (e.g., §92.207(b)(6) 'most integrated setting') until the delayed applicability date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on Sex Discrimination Related to Marital, Parental, or Family Status (§92.208)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits discrimination on the basis of marital, parental, or family status in relation to sex discrimination; addresses pregnancy-related conditions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The provision covers denial or limitation of services tied to marital/parental status and clarifies protections for pregnancy-related conditions consistent with statutory text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination on the Basis of Association (§92.209)
rubrics_metrics.description: Prohibits discrimination on the basis of association with protected classes (race, color, national origin, sex, age, disability).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entities may not deny services or otherwise discriminate against individuals because of their association with a protected individual or group.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination in the Use of Patient Care Decision Support Tools (§92.210)
rubrics_metrics.description: Requires covered entities to avoid discrimination arising from the use of patient care decision support tools (formerly 'clinical algorithms') and to take reasonable steps to mitigate discrimination once made aware of potential discrimination resulting from use of these tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR renamed 'clinical algorithms' to 'patient care decision support tools,' specified the scope of application, and required reasonable mitigation steps when potential for discrimination is identified; entities should assess tools for disparate impact by protected characteristics and remediate where necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nondiscrimination in Delivery of Health Programs/Activities Through Telehealth (§92.211)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applies nondiscrimination requirements to health programs and activities delivered through telehealth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions of telehealth were added/clarified; entities delivering telehealth must ensure meaningful access, effective communication, ICT accessibility, and nondiscriminatory program design in telehealth services.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enforcement Mechanisms (§92.301)
rubrics_metrics.description: Enforcement of the rule will use mechanisms provided under title VI, title IX, the Age Act, or section 504 as applicable for violations of section 1557.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The preamble and text explain how existing enforcement frameworks and remedies apply, including complaint investigations, technical assistance, and potential corrective actions; OCR indicated priorities for technical assistance during early implementation for some aspects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification of Views Regarding Application of Federal Religious Freedom and Conscience Laws (§92.302)
rubrics_metrics.description: Establishes a process for recipients to notify OCR of views regarding the application of Federal religious freedom and conscience laws and allows recipients to request an assurance of an exemption, availability of temporary exemptions, and an administrative appeal process.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR modified §92.302 to clarify administrative process details and availability of temporary exemptions and appeals; recipients seeking exemptions should follow the process specified in the provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for Health Programs/Activities Conducted by Recipients and State Exchanges (§92.303)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies procedural obligations for enforcement, complaint handling, and administration for programs conducted by recipients and state Exchanges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides mechanics for how complaints are handled by recipients/state Exchanges; entities must follow procedural rules for notifications, investigations, and recordkeeping.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedures for Health Programs/Activities Administered by the Department (§92.304)
rubrics_metrics.description: Specifies procedures the Department will follow for programs administered directly by HHS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes procedural details for Department-administered programs including investigations, notices, and remedial steps; aligns Department procedures with enforcement mechanisms described elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Change in Interpretation: Medicare Part B as Federal Financial Assistance
rubrics_metrics.description: HHS provides official notice that Medicare Part B funding meets the definition of 'Federal financial assistance' for purposes of civil rights enforcement under section 1557.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This interpretation expands the universe of programs and activities subject to section 1557 nondiscrimination obligations and affects enforcement and coverage determinations; comments and responses are provided in section III of the preamble.

rubrics_metrics.name: CMS Amendments to Medicaid/CHIP/PACE/Exchanges/Issuer Standards
rubrics_metrics.description: CMS is finalizing amendments to its regulations to implement changes consistent with section 1557, including revising scope of sex discrimination to be consistent with §92.101(a)(2), non-interference provisions, standards of conduct for Federally-Facilitated Exchanges, Essential Health Benefits nondiscrimination, QHP participation standards, and direct enrollment rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: CMS amendments affect Exchanges, issuers, agents/brokers/web-brokers, and application of nondiscrimination to benefit design, issuer participation, network adequacy, and direct enrollment; affected entities should review specific CFR changes cited (45 CFR 147.104, 155.120, 155.220, 156.125, 156.200, 156.1230) and implementation timelines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Delayed Applicability and Compliance Timing (benefit design and procedural items)
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain provisions that would require changes to health insurance or group health plan benefit design have a delayed applicability date: the first day of the first plan year beginning on or after January 1, 2025 for coverage newly subject to the rule; certain procedural provisions have phased applicability to allow time for compliance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: newly-covered group health plans offering non-calendar year plans have until their first plan year beginning on/after Jan 1, 2025; Notice of Availability has a 1-year delayed applicability; OCR will examine whether coverage was subject to the 2020 Rule for complaints received prior to Jan 1, 2025.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recordkeeping: Grievance Retention and Documentation
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities with 15 or more employees must retain grievance complaints for no less than three years; all covered entities must document employee training on section 1557.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regulatory Impact Analysis provides estimates of affected entities and time burdens; entities should maintain records to demonstrate compliance and facilitate enforcement reviews.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to Mitigate Discrimination from Decision Support Tools
rubrics_metrics.description: When made aware of the potential for discrimination resulting from use of patient care decision support tools, covered entities must take reasonable steps to mitigate that discrimination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR expects covered entities to assess tools for disparate impact, adjust algorithms/tools or their use as needed, and document mitigation actions; this applies to 'patient care decision support tools' as newly defined.
